content:
The new Apple TV 4K has been a long time coming—it was originally expected to launch last fall. But with Siri AI finally ready to go, all signs point to a new Apple TV 4K making an appearance, possibly unveiled at the September 9 event. Here are the rumors currently circulating.

#1: Siri Remote Update

Although no details have been revealed yet, Apple is reportedly preparing an updated Siri Remote for the new Apple TV 4K.

Code leaked in the macOS 26.7 beta appears to confirm the existence of a new Siri Remote. And before that leak, Mark Gurman reported that the new hardware 'might' come with a 'tweaked Apple TV remote'.

The changes don't seem to be major. But hopefully it will at least include a second-generation ultra-wideband chip to support precision finding.

#2: Siri AI and More Apple Intelligence Features

Siri AI is expected to be one of the key selling points for the new Apple TV and other new home products.

So far, Apple has not announced whether the new assistant will come to Apple TV 4K or HomePod. But mounting evidence suggests that tvOS 27 will include Siri AI built-in, and likely only on the new hardware.

Other Apple Intelligence features are also expected to roll out alongside, such as a more powerful search experience.

#3: All-New A-Series Chip

The current Apple TV uses an A15 Bionic chip, which first debuted in 2021. Fortunately, the new model is expected to see a significant performance upgrade.

It's said to use a more powerful new A-series chip to support AI features.

Rumors suggest it could be the A17 Pro or A18. But those reports mostly predate the arrival of Siri AI. It wouldn't be surprising for Apple to go straight with a more powerful A19 or A20 on the new hardware.

#4: N1 Wireless Chip

Most Liked Comment by Doug

So ideally, it should be able to replace my older HomePod setup to support Siri AI.

Second, it should have built-in microphones so I can issue Siri AI commands without needing to use the remote.

Finally, it should deliver on the long-promised universal TV controller feature (previously blocked by partners like Netflix) so I can search across all my services in one place for new shows—including my cable provider.

Netflix's catalog data is public, so Siri AI could search it alongside all my other media services. Apple TV should be the universal set-top box.

Also, AirPlay should have supported connecting to multiple HomePods long ago for a perfect home theater setup—I mean automatically calibrated Atmos sound.

The N1 wireless chip first appeared on the iPhone 17, and there are also rumors it will be used in the new Apple TV 4K.

With the N1 chip, Apple TV will support Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, as well as Thread networking.

By comparison, the existing Apple TV hardware is already four years old and only supports Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.

What features would you like to see in the new Apple TV 4K? Let us know in the comments.
